scan_result: A concrete historical-edition scan candidate exists: Müller, FHG II (1848), Internet Archive `fragmentahistori02unse`; its repository README records 360 ppi, 690 images, and visually acceptable Greek samples. The catalogue puts Megasthenes at pp. 397–439, while the Canon’s separate 1489.003 specifies pp. 402–439; page-to-fragment correspondence and copy-level rights remain to be checked.
scan_rights: Underlying 1848 edition is public domain; Internet Archive shows no explicit digitisation licence, so the image set is not admitted yet.
next_action: Treat 1489.003 as the historically matching Müller edition; verify its images/page mapping and reuse terms before any image-only acquisition. For 1489.002, compare FGrH 715 fragments against that earlier edition without conflating editions.
notes: The lost Indica survives only through many host authors. The source scan is relevant but cannot substitute automatically for Jacoby’s later FGrH arrangement. No third-party OCR or image was retrieved.
